# Introduction

A trajectory inference tool orders the cells of a single-cell RNA-seq
experiment along a pseudotime and splits them into branching paths, such as
the paths from a progenitor to two cell types. scMaSigPro finds the genes
whose expression changes along the pseudotime of a path and the genes whose
expression differs between paths [@srivastava2024]. It brings the
method of the maSigPro package for time-course experiments
[@conesa2006; @nueda2014] to single cells in two steps:

1. The cells of each path are pooled into bins along pseudotime, and their
    counts are added up into pseudo-bulk counts. The bins play the part of the
    time points of a time-course experiment.
2. A polynomial generalised linear model in the binned pseudotime, with one
    set of terms per path, is fitted to the pseudo-bulk counts of each gene,
    by default with a negative binomial distribution and an offset for the
    sequencing depth of each bin. The genes whose model is better than a flat
    line, and the terms that make it so, tell how a gene changes along each
    path.

This vignette runs these steps on `splat.sim`, a small data set bundled with
the package. The other vignettes go further:

* [Trajectory input](
    https://spriyansh.github.io/scMaSigPro/articles/trajectory-input.html):
    pseudotime and path labels from slingshot, Monocle3 or another tool.
* [Shared root](
    https://spriyansh.github.io/scMaSigPro/articles/shared-root.html):
    trajectories whose paths share their first cells.
* [Model and tuning](
    https://spriyansh.github.io/scMaSigPro/articles/model-and-tuning.html):
    the model, its settings and how they change the results.
* [maSigPro and the ScMaSigPro class](
    https://spriyansh.github.io/scMaSigPro/articles/masigpro-and-class.html):
    the object, its accessors and the equivalence with maSigPro.
* [Frequently asked questions](
    https://spriyansh.github.io/scMaSigPro/articles/faq.html).

# Installation

scMaSigPro is installed from GitHub with BiocManager, which also installs
its Bioconductor dependencies:

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("BioBam/scMaSigPro")
```

# The data

`splat.sim` is a `SingleCellExperiment` with the counts of 100 genes in 200
cells, simulated with splatter [@zappia2017] along two paths that
start from the same cells. Each cell has a simulated step along its path,
which serves as its pseudotime, and the label of its path.

```{r load-data, message = FALSE}
library(scMaSigPro)
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(ggplot2)

data("splat.sim", package = "scMaSigPro")
splat.sim
head(colData(splat.sim)[, c("Step", "Group")])
```

The first two principal components show the two paths, `Path1` and `Path2`,
leaving the same starting cells:

```{r plot-pca, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
#| fig.alt: >
#|   Principal components of splat.sim: the cells of Path1 and Path2 leave the
#|   same starting cells, coloured from low to high step.
pca <- as.data.frame(reducedDim(splat.sim, "PCA"))
pca$Step <- colData(splat.sim)$Step
pca$Path <- colData(splat.sim)$Group
ggplot(pca, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, colour = Step, shape = Path)) +
    geom_point() +
    scale_colour_viridis_c() +
    theme_minimal()
```

# The workflow

## Create the object

scMaSigPro keeps the data and every result in an object of class
`ScMaSigPro`. `as_scmp()` creates it from a `SingleCellExperiment` whose
cell metadata holds the pseudotime and the path of each cell; here they are
the `Step` and `Group` columns. `create_scmp()` does the same from a count
matrix and a table of cell metadata.

```{r create-object}
scmp_ob <- as_scmp(
    object = splat.sim,
    verbose = FALSE,
    additional_params = list(
        labels_exist = TRUE,
        exist_ptime_col = "Step",
        exist_path_col = "Group"
    )
)
scmp_ob
```

## Bin the cells along pseudotime

`sc.squeeze()` divides the pseudotime of each path into bins of equal width
and adds up the counts of the cells of each bin. The number of bins comes
from a histogram rule, by default that of Sturges, log~2~(n) + 1 bins for
the n cells of a path, rounded up.

```{r squeeze}
scmp_ob <- sc.squeeze(scmp_ob)
bins <- cDense(scmp_ob)
table(bins$Path)
```

The `r nrow(bins)` bins hold between `r min(bins$scmp_bin_size)` and
`r max(bins$scmp_bin_size)` cells. `plotBinTile()` shows the number of cells
of each bin along the binned pseudotime of each path:

```{r plot-bins, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3}
#| fig.alt: >
#|   Tile plot of the bins of Path1 and Path2 along binned pseudotime, coloured
#|   by the number of cells of each bin.
plotBinTile(scmp_ob)
```

## Set up the polynomial model

`sc.set.poly()` builds the design of the model. With two paths and a
polynomial of degree 1, the model of the expected count of a gene in a bin
is

$$
\log(\mu) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 D + \beta_2 t + \beta_3 t D + \text{offset},
$$

where $t$ is the binned pseudotime and $D$ is 1 for the bins of `Path2` and
0 for those of `Path1`, the reference path. $\beta_0$ and $\beta_2$ describe
the reference path; $\beta_1$ and $\beta_3$ are the differences of `Path2`
from it, at the start and in slope.

```{r set-poly}
scmp_ob <- sc.set.poly(scmp_ob, poly_degree = 1)
showPoly(scmp_ob)
```

A higher degree adds the squares, cubes and so on of $t$ and their products
with $D$, for profiles that rise and fall; the
[Model and tuning](
    https://spriyansh.github.io/scMaSigPro/articles/model-and-tuning.html)
vignette compares degrees.

## Find the genes that change

`sc.p.vector()` fits the full model of each gene and tests it against a
model with the intercept only, a flat profile. The genes whose adjusted
p-value is at most `p_value` have a non-flat profile.

```{r p-vector}
scmp_ob <- sc.p.vector(scmp_ob, p_value = 0.05, verbose = FALSE)
res <- scmpResults(scmp_ob)
sum(res$non_flat)
```

`r sum(res$non_flat)` of the `r nrow(res)` genes have a non-flat profile.

## Select the significant terms

`sc.t.fit()` then removes, one at a time, the terms of the model of each of
these genes that are not significant (backward stepwise selection). What is
left says how the gene changes: a gene with only $\beta_3$ besides the
intercept, for example, has the same expression in both paths at the start
but a different slope.

```{r t-fit}
scmp_ob <- sc.t.fit(scmp_ob, verbose = FALSE)
head(showSol(scmp_ob)[, c("p-value", "R-squared")])
```

## List the significant genes

`sc.filter()` keeps the genes whose selected model explains enough of their
variation, measured by its R-squared, and sorts them into lists. With
`vars = "groups"` there is one list per path: the list of the reference path
holds the genes that change along it, and the list `Path2vsPath1` the genes
whose profile in `Path2` differs from that in `Path1`.

```{r filter}
scmp_ob <- sc.filter(scmp_ob, rsq = 0.7, vars = "groups")
res <- scmpResults(scmp_ob)
table(Path1 = res$sig_Path1, Path2vsPath1 = res$sig_Path2vsPath1)
```

The genes in both lists change along `Path1` and differ in `Path2`; those
only in `Path2vsPath1` are flat in `Path1` but change in `Path2`; those only
in `Path1` change along it in the same way in both paths.

`plotIntersect()` shows how the lists overlap; it draws an UpSet plot with
the UpSetR package [@conway2017]:

```{r plot-intersect, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
#| fig.alt: >
#|   UpSet plot of the gene lists Path1 and Path2vsPath1: the size of each list
#|   and of their intersection.
plotIntersect(scmp_ob)
```

```{r lists, include = FALSE}
both <- rownames(res)[res$sig_Path1 & res$sig_Path2vsPath1]
only_diff <- rownames(res)[!res$sig_Path1 & res$sig_Path2vsPath1]
only_ref <- rownames(res)[res$sig_Path1 & !res$sig_Path2vsPath1]
```

## Plot gene trends

`plotTrend()` draws the pseudo-bulk counts of a gene, divided by the size
factor of their bin, on the log scale against the binned pseudotime, with
the fitted curve of each path. Here is one gene of each kind:

```{r plot-trends, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
#| fig.alt: >
#|   Trends of three genes: one that changes in Path1 and differs in Path2, one
#|   flat in Path1 that changes in Path2, and one that changes in the same way
#|   in both paths.
genes <- c(both[1], only_diff[1], only_ref[1])
plots <- lapply(genes, function(g) plotTrend(scmp_ob, g, lines = TRUE))
patchwork::wrap_plots(plots, ncol = 2)
```

## Cluster the trends

`sc.cluster.trend()` groups the genes of the lists by the coefficients of
their models, here with hierarchical clustering into four clusters; k-means
and the model-based clustering of mclust [@scrucca2016] are the other
methods (`cluster_method`). `plotTrendCluster()` draws the trends of each
cluster:

```{r cluster, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
#| fig.alt: >
#|   Trends of the four clusters of genes, one panel per cluster, with the
#|   median profile of each path.
scmp_ob <- sc.cluster.trend(scmp_ob, geneSet = "union", k = 4)
plotTrendCluster(scmp_ob, verbose = FALSE)
```

## Get the results

`scmpResults()` returns every result with one row per gene: the p-value of
the full model and whether the profile is non-flat (`sc.p.vector()`), the
p-value and R-squared of the selected model and whether the gene has
influential observations (`sc.t.fit()`), one column per gene list
(`sc.filter()`) and the cluster (`sc.cluster.trend()`).

```{r results}
head(scmpResults(scmp_ob))
```

`scmpToRowData()` writes these columns, with the prefix `scmp_`, into the
`rowData()` of a `SingleCellExperiment`, so that they travel with the data:

```{r row-data}
splat.sim <- scmpToRowData(splat.sim, scmp_ob)
head(rowData(splat.sim)[, c("scmp_non_flat", "scmp_cluster")])
```

# Compare with the simulated truth

splatter stores in the `rowData()` how it simulated each gene. `DEFacPath1`
and `DEFacPath2` are the factors by which the expression of a gene changes
from the start to the end of each path: a gene whose factor is not 1 on a
path changes along that path. In `splat.sim` every such gene has different
factors on the two paths, so it also differs between them.

```{r truth}
truth <- rowData(splat.sim)
changes <- truth$DEFacPath1 != 1 | truth$DEFacPath2 != 1
names(changes) <- rownames(truth)
found <- scmpResults(scmp_ob)$non_flat
table(non_flat = found, simulated = changes[rownames(scmpResults(scmp_ob))])
```

```{r truth-numbers, include = FALSE}
tp <- sum(found & changes)
precision <- tp / sum(found)
recall <- tp / sum(changes)
```

Of the `r sum(found)` genes with a non-flat profile, `r tp` were simulated
to change (a precision of `r round(precision, 2)`), and they are
`r tp` of the `r sum(changes)` genes simulated to change (a recall of
`r round(recall, 2)`). The
[Model and tuning](
    https://spriyansh.github.io/scMaSigPro/articles/model-and-tuning.html)
vignette shows how the settings move these numbers.

The trends of the plotted genes follow the factors of the simulation:

```{r truth-genes}
as.data.frame(truth[genes, c("DEFacPath1", "DEFacPath2")])
```

The bundled object `scmp.ob` holds the result of this workflow, so the
examples of the help pages and the other vignettes can start from it:

```{r scmp-ob}
data("scmp.ob", package = "scMaSigPro")
identical(scmpResults(scmp.ob), scmpResults(scmp_ob))
```
